basis: Codex GPFH (CXC 1-1969) 13.2.8: incoming material known to carry microbiological contaminants that cannot be reduced to an acceptable level must not be accepted; visible mold is such microbiological spoilage.
Food Safety Act 2013 s34 prohibits producing, storing or selling decomposed fish, meat, milk, egg or foods made from them; a slimy surface is a typical decomposition sign.
Food Safety Act 2013 s26 bans food that is sub-standard for human consumption; abnormal discoloration indicates deterioration to sub-standard condition.
Codex GPFH (CXC 1-1969) 13.2.8: raw materials are visually inspected for packages damaged during transportation; a bloated package signals gas-producing contamination and must not be accepted.
Codex GPFH (CXC 1-1969) 13.2.8: incoming material is inspected visually for packages damaged during transportation and material known to be contaminated is not accepted.
Food Safety Act 2013 s34 bans decomposed milk and egg; curdling or unexpected liquid separation is a decomposition sign.
Food Safety Act 2013 s26 bans food that is sub-standard for human consumption; unexpected foam or bubbles indicate unwanted fermentation or contamination.
Codex GPFH (CXC 1-1969) 13.2.5: systems must prevent extraneous hard or sharp objects such as glass or metal from reaching food; food containing foreign matter is not acceptable.
Food Safety Act 2013 s29 prohibits storing, supplying or selling any food after its expiry date; s32(c) requires packaged food labels to state the expiry date.

Codex CXC 52-2003 s4: fish known to contain toxic, decomposed or extraneous substances must not be accepted and unfit fish must be removed and disposed of; seafood dishes warrant particular attention to freshness and time/temperature control.
National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 2 (diabetes mellitus), p.69: for type-2 diabetes, sodium restriction varies with health status, usually in the range below 2000 mg/day.

National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 7 (hypertension), p.81: consume sodium below 1.5 g (with fibre 30 g, cholesterol 150 mg); reduce salt intake to less than 1 tsp/day, preferably three-quarters of a teaspoon.

National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 2, p.68-69: restrict foods containing fat and oil as people with diabetes are at higher risk of coronary heart disease, and prefer low-fat methods such as boiling, steaming and grilling.

National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 2 (fats and oils), p.19: limit the intake of deep-fried foods and oily snacks; trans fats in fried and processed foods increase the risk of coronary heart disease.
